text:
Sam: Heads-up — noticed a regression in prod after the 8x7B kernel-selector tweak. p95 token latency jumped ~3x for a subset of requests that cross the max_pos boundary. :eyes:
perf-bot: alert: reroute-alert — service=redwood-hosted model=mistral-8x7b route=stable latency_p95=312ms (+220ms)
Jin: same here in bench runs. Repro steps: long chat turns that push sequence length past 4096 cause the runtime to flip from fused_attn -> fallback_scaled_attn which is way slower. Logs show kernel_choice=fallback_scaled_attn and kv_cache_hits dropping to 0 when windowing kicks in.
Mira: attached quick profiling (nvprof snippet):
```
GPU kernel timeline:
 fused_attn_forward  0.8ms
 fused_attn_backward 1.2ms
 fallback_scaled_attn 4.1ms  <-- hot
 kv_cache_load 0.2ms
```
Also saw lots of small kernels after batcher splits windows: kernel-launch overhead + small tile kernels.
Sam: interestingly it's not consistent — only when requests have mixed sequence lengths in the same batch (some already at 2048, some at 4600). Batcher heuristics are mixing windowed and full sequences.
Jin: hypothesis: the kernel selector uses a heuristic that disables fused path when "sliding_window" flag present or when seq_len > max_kernel_seq. Because the batch contains both, selector conservatively picks fallback. We should either: (a) group by effective seq_len before kernel selection, or (b) allow fused kernel if most of batch fits and fallback for remainder (partial-grid).
Mira: I dumped the kernel-selector decision trace: 
```
ks.decide(batch_shapes=[2048,2048,4600,4600], model=mistral-8x7b)
-> decision: fallback_scaled_attn (reason: mixed_seq_lengths, sliding_window=true)
```
We could change the decision to do sub-batching by seq_len buckets which avoids fallback for the 2048s.
Sam: batching change sounds low-risk. Another lever: RoPE scale interacts — for sequences crossing the boundary we rescale RoPE to avoid wrap, and that currently toggles a different matmul path because we switch to int8-friendly quant codepath. Might be two independent factors.
Jin: confirmed. When RoPE_rescale=true the kernel selector appends "quant-safe" tag which blocks fused_attn. That was added to be safe for q4_* models, but it looks overly conservative for these M8x7B QK dims.
Mira: quick experiment: patch local kernel selector to ignore RoPE tag for model="mistral-8x7b" and rerun bench. Result: p95 for mixed batch dropped from 312ms -> 140ms. Throughput stable.
Sam: nice. Can we make a minimal config change: allow rope-rescale tolerant fused kernel when head_dim % 64 == 0 and kv_dim==... (add rule). Share config snippet?
Mira: draft rule I used: 
```
kernel_selector.rules.allow_fused_if:
  - model=="mistral-8x7b"
  - sliding_window in [true,false]  # don't block for sliding
  - (rope_rescale == true) -> allow_if(head_dim % 64 == 0)
  - mixed_seq_strategy: bucket_by_seq_len
```
It reduced kernel churn and kept correctness in our eval prompts.
Jin: batching heuristic PR idea: implement bucket_by_window_index where we group by (seq_len // window_size) so windows across different original lengths align. That reduces unique seq_len variants in a batch. Also add small coalescing threshold: if a seq_len bucket has <10% of batch, put them in their own sub-batch so they don't force fallback.
Sam: owners: @Jin will prototype batcher bucketing and perf harness, @Sam will open a kernel-selector config PR with Mira's rule, @Mira will run canary on dedicated pool and run QA prompts for RoPE accuracy. :hammer_and_wrench:
Mira: I ran the QA prompt set — no measurable quality regressions for rescale tolerance on M8x7B and M7B. We should still add a short eval to guard against subtle phase shifts.
perf-bot: bench results (canary): mistral-8x7b mixed-batch p95=142ms, p50=28ms, kv_cache_hit_rate=98%
Jin: next steps: 1) add sub-batching bucket_by_seq_len (PR#2345), 2) relax RoPE blocklist in selector config (PR#2346), 3) run 24h canary on dedicated cluster and monitor tail latencies + token quality evals.
Sam: I'll coordinate the rollouts — will put both PRs behind feature flags and do a staged canary. If anyone sees mismatch or quality drift, ping here and rollback plan is to flip the feature flag off.
Mira: repro curl for bench (use test api key):
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer test-KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"mistral-8x7b","input":"<long prompt that forces >4096>","max_tokens":100}'
```
Expect the logs to show `kernel_choice` entries per sub-batch — confirm fused_attn for the 2k windows.
Jin: I'll run 1k sample load and post flamegraph link once done.
Sam: perfect. Thanks all — this looks actionable. We'll track in the reroute incident and close once the 24h canary is green. :white_check_mark:
